note: v3409: Every law here was named by the CROSS-FAMILY REVIEW of v3404, reading the shipped diff cold, and all four were real. _pull_once ran git fetch and git merge --ff-only and read NEITHER return code, so an offline fetch, a credential refusal, a lock held by fleet_origin_status on the SAME 300s cadence, a diverged history or a refused fast-forward all left HEAD unmoved - and moved is False for nothing-to-do and for it-did-not-work alike, so the lane published already-level, the one sentence it must never say falsely. git status exit 128 with EMPTY stdout is how git reports dubious ownership or a held lock, and reading only stdout turned each into go-ahead-and-pull on a console that execs the working tree. The heart row dated behind from FETCH_HEAD, which a fetch of any OTHER ref rewrites - and the obvious fix was WORSE, measured before it shipped: the ref mtime made the row read MISSING 32.1h on a machine that had fetched minutes earlier, because a fetch bringing nothing new never rewrites the ref. Both ages are reported now and neither answers the other question. Three checks added in ONE session shipped with no WATCHES declaration, reading ABSENT in the organ table. AND THE GATE WIDENING BLINDED ITSELF: accepting the door new home _gq.run also accepted the bare name run, which is what subprocess.run is called, so heart2 reported BLIND - stayed GREEN through its own defeat. Un-blinding it found a THIRD git spawn nobody had seen. 20 git argv sites across 2 files now walk ONE door in tv/git_quiet.py, and there may only ever be one body of it.
